messages:
maria_support: Customer reported weird embed cache hits returning 1024-d vectors while their app is configured for text-embedding-3-large (1536). They see tokenized billing for large model but cached vectors are short. They also report intermittent 400/422 when batch size changes.

sam_ml: Hmm. Two common failure modes: keying doesn't include model version or an encoding/quantization step strips dims. Do we know their cache key scheme?

maria_support: They provided this snippet of how they call our API and then lookup our internal cache key: 
```
key = f"emb:{tenant_id}:{prefix}"
# prefix is user-supplied up to now
emb = cache.get(key)
if not emb:
    emb = call_redwood_embedding(model, texts)
    cache.set(key, emb, ttl=3600)
```
They suspect the prefix they use is reused across products.

jin_prod: Oof. That key doesn't include model or embedding dimension, so if the same prefix was used with another model (or older quantized pipeline) you'll mix dims. Tenant isolation is there but same tenant + reused prefix across different callers will collide.

kevin_billing: Customer also flagged billing anomalies — charged for large model tokens even when cached result was small vector. That suggests cache hit returned older small-model vectors but we still billed for the large model call?

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0947. Assigned to sam_ml, priority P2.

sam_ml: Repro plan: 1) Create two synthetic pipelines under same tenant using different models (text-embedding-3-small -> 1536? wait small vs large dims vary; confirm dims) 2) Use identical prefix value for both 3) Hit embedding endpoint then verify cache.get returns vector length mismatch and billing logs show model used per request.

maria_support: Customer gave concrete example: they called text-embedding-3-small previously and stored result under prefix "product:faq:v1". Later they migrated to text-embedding-3-large and kept same prefix. After a deploy, calls returned cached 1536? No actually the bug: sometimes returned 1536 and sometimes 1024 based on backend worker. They see TTL=1h, but multiple workers with different transform pipelines existed.

sam_ml: Let's capture precise dims: text-embedding-3-small -> 1536, text-embedding-3-large -> 3072 (hypothetical). But their report had 1024 vs 1536; maybe they used an older internal model with 1024. I need exact model names and dims from logs. maria can you attach customer headers: model name and request id?

maria_support: Provided headers: Model: text-embed-v2-1024, Request-Id: r-0a7b12c4, Time: 2026-02-12T15:42:01Z. Later call with same prefix: Model: text-embedding-3-large, Request-Id: r-0a7b12d0, Time: 2026-02-12T15:45:25Z. Cache returned length 1024 vector on the second call.

sam_ml: That proves it. Cache key lacked model identifier AND our cache terrain had a stale pre-quantized pipeline hanging around that returned the older dim. Root cause: prefix-only keying + multiple worker image variants.

jin_prod: Short-term mitigation: include model name + version + dim in cache key to avoid cross-model collisions. Also invalidate TTL for prefixes where we detect dim mismatch on read.

sam_ml: Agreed. Also add assert on read: if emb.shape != expected_dim then evict and log a metric (emb_cache_key_dim_mismatch).

maria_support: Customer is worried about billing. kevin_billing, can we retroactively reconcile if they were billed for large-model calls but received cached small vectors?

kevin_billing: We'll need to correlate request-ids to billing ledger. If a request used cached result but our billing pipeline recorded the model from the request rather than the cache hit, then they were billed correctly (for large model) even though they got small vector — they were overcharged for quality mismatch. We can offer one-time credit after validation. Ask customer for sample request-ids (they provided a few).

ops-bot: Automation suggestion: add cache key hashing that includes \"model_name\" and \"vector_dim\" in addition to tenant+prefix.

sam_ml: I'll push a quick patch to embedding cache key function in runtime: 
```
def make_cache_key(tenant, prefix, model_name, dim):
    return f"emb:{tenant}:{model_name}:{dim}:{prefix}"
```
And add a read-time check: if stored_dim != expected_dim => evict and set metric.

jin_prod: Also need to rollout across workers atomically or with a migration script to avoid transient double-keys causing inconsistent hits. Plan: 1) Deploy read-evict behavior (safe) 2) Deploy writer change to write new key format 3) Run a background migration to re-key popular prefixes.

maria_support: Customer asked for repro steps so they can test before we change prod. Provide them a minimal curl that simulates collision: 
```bash
# simulate write by older pipeline
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"old-embed-1024","input":["test"] , "prefix":"product:faq:v1"}'
# then call with new model using same prefix
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["test"] , "prefix":"product:faq:v1"}'
```
Expect second call: either evict+recompute or return mismatched dim depending on current runtime.

sam_ml: Also note batching: If they send batched requests with mixed models accidentally, our router should reject mixes. Add validation: batch.model must be uniform — return 400 if mismatched. That explains intermittent 400/422 when their client changed batch payloads.

maria_support: Customer is okay with credits if we confirm billing mismatch. They asked for ETA on fix for keying change.

sam_ml: I'll have the read-evict patch and metric in staging today, deploy to canary tomorrow. Full rollout after migration script — estimate 3 days. I'll add a PR with tests showing evict on dim mismatch.

jin_prod: I'll coordinate the migration job and ensure observability (metric + trace link) so support can confirm in real-time.

kevin_billing: Once we have request-id mapping and confirmation from sam, we can offer pro-rated credit. Keep me looped with request-ids.

maria_support: Thanks everyone. Forwarding repro and mitigation steps to the customer now.

ops-bot: INC-2026-0947 updated: sam_ml assigned, status in progress.
